utterances.text: Thank you. You saw these engines, and you say that they were four metres long; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: That's right. I am shocked by the size of these engines. I remember that in Geteova Street number 5, I remember that there were the remains of this rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 36, you say: "If the victim was hit indoors, the first thing to establish is the place where the bullet pierced the window or the door." And you say you can never rule out the possibility that the bullet was fired inside; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Well, when I gave this statement, since it was an extensive one and it involves a great many cases, when one comes to a particular site and if a corpse is found in an apartment, for instance, we establish that the said person was killed by a bullet, and we have to establish how that happened. Between 1992 and 1995, when people were being killed by rifle bullets, when we would find corpses, when witnesses would report that, or somebody else, we'd see traces on windows and walls and so on. Photographs would be taken. And then on the basis of the actual bullet, we would determine whether that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You rightly conclude that only one straight line can be drawn through two points and that in order to establish the direction, you need two points for the line of the projectile to be established?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, only one straight line can be drawn between two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 38, you say: "In most of these cases, the bodies or the injured were taken away before I arrived on site. It is necessary to examine the injuries on a body to establish the direction and distance of fire, and that job was done by the Forensic Department." Is that right? Or see what it says further on: "In order to be able to establish the origin of fire, you need at least two points for bullets coming in ..." You used a kind of string, right, to establish the direction of fire; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: That's right, a string would be used. Things are a bit more modern today, but we would use a string, when there would be two or three different points through which a string could be drawn, in order to have the exact direction of fire established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 39, you say: "A bullet can ricochet and change direction in a room. A forensic expert can say if the bullet entered the body directly or after a ricochet -- whether it entered the body before or after ricochet." And then in paragraph 40, then you say that: "In sniping incidents that happened outside, we had to talk to witnesses, in order to find out the position of the victim, or to the victim if he or she was still alive." So your task and your duty was to establish whether the bullet had ricochetted before entering a body, and if that happened outdoors, you had to ask the witnesses how the body was positioned in order to determine the direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Well, yes, in the cases -- and I'm talking about criminal investigation technicians. I don't know of any case of someone being hit outdoors. But, in any case, the on-site investigation had to be carried out. If there was only a blood-stain, then it would be only a blood-stain. The inspectors would have to interview witnesses and ask them about where the projectile came. If we had a situation where the bullet ricochetted against a surface, it might have happened that as a result of ricochetting, it hit a victim. Now, my task indoors was to collect all the clothes relating to the points of entry of the bullet, whether it came through the window, through the window-pane, and also to detect all the traces left inside the flat. If there was no possibility for me to connect these two points, it might have been a bullet, but if it didn't have enough impact, it could have ricochetted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to make it clear to me: If a bullet passes through a body, did you take into account the fact that that can also affect the trajectory and the ricochetting?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Of course, we took that into account. But then, again, it depended on the power of the bullet passing through a body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You pointed out the importance of interviews of witnesses in the cases of outdoor sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I think that was referred to in my first statement given to this Tribunal. And I would like to underline, once again, that I did not conduct this on-site investigation on my own. At least one inspector from the CSB would accompany me, and he would be in charge of examining witnesses and interviewing people related to the incident in whatever way. But it was never my job to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I am a bit perplexed by paragraph 41, where you say that: "On the basis of the entry and exit wound on the body, it was possible to establish if the victim was directly targeted or was just hit at random, for if a victim is directly targeted, the line between the entry and exit wound is straight, but if the bullet just is losing its power and falling, there is a parabolic line." How is it possible to establish a parabolic line inside a body, between the entry and exit wounds?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Only a forensic medical doctor can give you an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, but this is what is said in your statement. So you believe that if they are at the same level, I mean, these two wounds, with respect to what, the ground or whatever, then the bullet must have gone straight -- in a straight line and that the victim was intentionally hit. However, if the entry and exit wounds are not at the same level, we have the case of random shooting?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Well, you see, during an investigation, if a pathologist conducted an autopsy, it was his duty and job to establish what kind of wounds were in question, whether it was a big or small wound, or what kind of damage it caused to the tissue, et cetera. So all these findings are contained in their reports. As I said, I gave a general statement, but I touched upon some of the investigations and instances in which I attended autopsies. However, the official findings is provided by a forensic medical doctor. He can say that the damage that a bullet causes to the body is not the result of a direct hit, but rather of a ricochet. Based on such findings is the fact that I made this kind of statement. So it was not up to me to decide whether the line was straight or parabolic; it is up to the forensic doctor to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As a young doctor, I also had to conduct autopsies, and I remember them quite clearly, but I cannot remember seeing anywhere, in any findings, the opinion of the pathologist performing the post-mortem that the line in the body was parabolic or otherwise. Can you help us locate any such report in which the pathologist had determined that the victim was intentionally targeted, due to the fact that the line was straight, or that it was shot randomly because the line was parabolic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: No, I don't have a single such forensic report. We can talk about this. I may be wrong, but, as I said, it's up to the forensic expert to say that. The fact that I gave this statement doesn't mean that I conducted post-mortem. If we are going to determine whether a hit was random or intentional, we can base that on the ricochet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I note the time. If it is convenient, shall we take a break now for 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are working in one-hour sessions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, only for today we will be sitting until 6.30. We'll break for 20 minutes. But before that, yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me, Mr. President. In connection with the testimony of Mr. Hogan, would we have -- I'd like to make an oral motion that Dr. Subotic be allowed to be in the courtroom during his testimony and participate to the extent she does with other witnesses. He's going to be testifying about locations in Sarajevo and incidents -- the shelling and sniping incidents, and she's worked on those more than anyone on our team, and it would be useful for her to assist Dr. Karadzic with his cross-examination of Mr. Hogan, if the Court would allow it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it also due to the absence of Mr. Sladojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's also another consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume at half past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic, regarding your request made at the end of the last session: At this moment, considering the nature of Mr. Hogan's expected evidence, and along with financial issues, the Chamber is not in a position to make that decision. If you are minded to tender a detailed submission in writing, the Chamber will consider it. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, we'll go back to your statements to look at specific incidents, but now I'd like to ask you: Do you know Dobrinja and its residents very well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I know Dobrinja, as a neighbourhood, very well, but I don't know the residents. It's just too broad a concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Dobrinja is not really very large, it's about a kilometre in length and 500 metres in width, about half a kilometre square?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I didn't measure, but I know it's divided into Dobrinja 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, and maybe if you include the airport settlement in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know which ABiH army forces were located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I don't know exactly up to what line, but I believe the 5th Motorised Brigade was there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the one that was later renamed 155th. But do you know a MUP unit called Bosna that was located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I heard of it, this Bosna unit. I believe it's a unit of the federal police, but where in Dobrinja they were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Kenan Ademovic, or perhaps Kemal, their commander?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I heard the name, but I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sejo Saric?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sime Sevabic [phoen], Muhamed Gafic [phoen], Delalic, Halilovic, Ibro Krakonja, did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Commander of the 1st Company, Mustafa Tabak; 2nd Company, Musan; and the 4th Company, Jusanovic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You worked on that sniping incident in Dobrinja where Jasmina Tabakovic was the victim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had another witness here from the list referring to that incident, so could we see 65 ter 09766 without broadcasting. 09766, broadcast, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us if these four persons really did this on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have to if it's not broadcast, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And let us continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, what was your job in this investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: My task, as a scenes-of-crime officer, was to photograph. Standard procedure in such investigations; to find traces left by the bullet in this case, to find the bullet, if possible, to be sent for further examination by experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You came to the scene on the following day? The entire team came on the following day?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If that's written here. And it is written, that we came to the scene on the following day. The event happened on the 14th of May, around 2345 hours, and we came the next morning, because it was impossible to do so immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was the ballistics expert on this team? In other words, who determined the trajectory?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: All I can see here is the investigating judge, the operations officer from the Homicide Department, an operations officer from the Novi Grad SJB, and myself, as forensic technician. I found the bullet, and I made the report about the investigation once it was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't mention in this report that you made any measurements. You just say that the projectile was fired from a fire-arm from Bosnian Serb positions and that such and such a woman found her death in the apartment of her parents. Why did you not mention those elements and the method of measurement in the report?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: First of all, nobody ever asked me whether I drafted this report. I didn't. You can see, on the next page, who the author is. And in my own report, I noted the measurements I made in that apartment. You see who drafted the report. This man was part of the team. He was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in this case, you were the ballistics man?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I was the crime of -- crime scene technician who found the traces, who noted them properly, who made the measurements and established the facts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3045. This document may be removed. It's in evidence, I believe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I please ask you to identify on this map the Hamdije Kapidzica Street, Miroslava Krleze Street as well? Miroslava Krleze is under number 297, and I can show you a list that confirms that. Use the pen, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I can only put a circle around the area where it happened, because there are no street names here, just numbers, 297 and 463. It's normal in such maps. But whether the position of the streets is correct, I don't know. I can only put a circle around the area where these two streets are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Hamdije Kapidzica Street used to be the Nehru Street before?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I don't remember anymore, and it's very difficult to determine the location because the buildings are not drawn here. This a very imprecise map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just mark it, and then we'll look for it on Google.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: That's the location where this complex of buildings, this block of buildings was, including the apartment building where this woman, Jasmina Tabakovic, was killed. I believe it was across the street from this 297, in this street marked "463," but I'm not sure without a more precise map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this apartment in Hamdije Kapidzica Street, which at the time was called the Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I see the Hamdije Kapidzica Street on the map. What it was called before, I don't know. These are things that are easily verifiable. What is certain is that this was a residential block divided in two. One side belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska and the other side belonged to the ABiH army, and the residents were from both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Serbs are also Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, because of overlapping questions and answers, I think you need to pause and start again for your last question. Mr. Witness, given that you are -- both Mr. Karadzic and you are speaking the same language, the interpreters have difficult times interpreting your words, so please put a pause between the question and answer. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My mistake. I have experience with this already, so I'll try harder. On a split screen, can we see 1D3046 and leave 3045 on the other half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you would like to use this marking, it's impossible. So if you'd like to ask the witness to mark it again, then we can move, but I don't -- if you'd like to keep this marking by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we'll need new markings after the witness determines which street is which. We can do without this. I believe the witness will correct himself when he sees the street names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let us see 1D3046.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can we then see the Nehru Street, Nehruova, and Hamdije Kapidzica Street. Just a moment. We lost it now. Can we see the previous view. No, no, not the picture; the list. A bit larger. Can we scroll up a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you would like to see number 297?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but let's see the Nehru Street first. Now it's called Hamdije Kapidzica Street. It must be there under "N." This is Nedzarici. We need Dobrinja. Here is Miroslava Krleze Street, 297. It's underlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Yes. I see it on the list, and the number is 297.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down again to see Nehru Street underlined as well. No, up again, please. Please bear with me just a moment. Let's have a look at Hamdije Kapidzica Street and what its previous name was. It should be under "H."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in your report, it is stated as "Nehruova Street 10"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If that's what the report states, it must be, and if that's what the rest of the reports say, that must have been the name of the street at the moment of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we go back to the map, please, in order to locate it. I hope you will take my word for it, that what used to be Nehru's Street is now called Hamdije Kapidzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you not to mark such a large circle, but to mark Miroslava Krleze Street, 297. The other part must have been in the Muslim hands, but Miroslava Krleze, 297, was under Serb control, as you say?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Well, the map is now gone, and I can see that the pen is on. So Miroslava Krleze, 297 [marks]. And 463, that street used to be Armija Bosnia-Herzegovina Street, I'm circling that [marks], and the street in between was no-man's land.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Hamdije Kapidzica Street, can you mark the incident location where the building was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I am a bit confused, because on the map I see Hamdije Kapidzica Street in a different place, and 463 that I circled, this is where the building is where Jasmina Tabakovic was killed in the street. Hamdije Kapidzica is to the north of 463, somewhere around the middle of the map. I cannot mark Hamdije Kapidzica here; I can only mark 297 and 463.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you believe that the shooting was in between those two numbers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: It's not what I think; I'm positive, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But then in the report, there is no "463." We'll try to see what the name of that street used to be and what it is now, and it is certainly not Nehru's Street. 463, it is Trg Sabora Bosanskog, the Bosanskog Sabora Square, so it is not Nehru's Street. Could we find Nehru's Street in order to ascertain where it was you carried out the on-site investigation and where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: According to the map, this is where the street of the on-site investigation was. This is not a detailed map. We would have to come up with a detailed map, with all of the streets and buildings, so as to make it possible for me to locate the exact building. I know very well this part of the town. I told you I lived and grew up in Dobrinja, in Sarajevo, and I still carry out on-site investigations there. It is true that Sabora Bosanskog Square is there, as well as Miroslava Krleze Street, and this is the Kurta Sorta [phoen] Street taking you to Vojkovici. I know that area well. As for Hamdije Kapidzica Street, it is to the north of "463" on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Miroslava Krleze Street with a "1" and the place of the incident with a "2"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D893.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have 1D3047. It's a Google photograph of the area. I hope it will be easier to get your bearings on it so as to find the locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see everything you need to see now?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If I may have a moment to find my bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We see a roundabout in one of the squares?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Yes. The roundabout is used by the town buses or the bus terminal, to turn around. I'm trying to find Kurta Sorta Street. Yes, it's fine now. Kurta Sorta Street, that was on the previous map, links the airport and Vojkovici, and the street perpendicular to it, in between the buildings, is Miroslava Krleze Street, and that's where the apartment is where Jasmina Tabakovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please use a red or a blue pen now to mark Kurta Sorta Street, as well as Miroslava Krleze Street, Nehru's Street, and the building where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: The Kurta Sorta Street links the airport -- well, it's here [marks]. What I'm circling now is the building in Miroslava Krleze Street [marks]. And this building across the street, on both sides has -- has streets, but the street next to it should be Nehru's Street, as it was called at the time. The incident took place in an apartment, but it's difficult for me to pin-point its precise location now. In any case, in the buildings across the street, there was Jasmina Tabakovic's apartment. I can circle both buildings, and then later on you can use the exact address to find the exact location of the apartment. So it's between the two blocks. That's where the street is that we have been trying to locate so far. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm afraid that you marked what used to be Lukavicka Street instead of Kurta Sorta Street. It is adjacent to the airport. In any case, could you mark with "1" and "2" -- the places from which the fire came and, with a "2," the place that was targeted?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Place today's date and the number.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For your convenience or information, Witness, we believe that Miroslava Krleze Street is the one you marked and Hamdije Kapidzica Street is the third street parallel to it, it is longitudinal to the first street, and that the building is just next to the roundabout to the north-east, I believe. So you missed by far, it seems.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I don't know what you believe, but I noticed the roundabout. I know that mention was made of Hamdije Kapidzica Street. I do know, however, that I went to the apartment which was in the location I marked, and I wasn't alone. The whole team was there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether an on-site investigation took place on Nehru's Street number 10?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If the report states that it is "Nehru's Street 10," then it is, and that's what the name was at the time. Whether there were any name changes later on, that's something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll keep it as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Karadzic, I couldn't follow your previous question, that -- forgive my pronunciation, but Hamdije Kapidzica Street was parallel to this street. Can we take a look at the map, 1D3046, or we can up-load Exhibit D893.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, could we please have the name list again, which is 1D02182, just so as to be certain what the name of the street is. So I would need the list of street names again, 1D02182. Here is the list. This is the list that accompanies the map. The third from the bottom, Dzevaharlal Nehrua Street is now called Hamdije Kapidzica Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, when he says this is the list that accompanies the map, which map is he referring to? Because I don't think it's the list that accompanies the map he's been using so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, can you clarify it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "All the streets in Sarajevo, PDF secured, Adobe Reader."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The position is this: This a list of street names produced by the Karadzic Defence, I think, and we have previously indicated our reservations about this list. The list which accompanies the map that Mr. Karadzic has been using does not, as far as I can see, contain Nehru Street. So when Mr. Karadzic says that this list accompanies the map, that's actually inaccurate. That's -- that's the only point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that is the case. I think it's a photocopy of some part of the bigger map. Mr. Witness, you are not in position to confirm whether Hamdije Kapidzica Street is a name of old Dzevaharlal Nehrua?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am certain that if, in our reports, we mentioned that it was Nehru's Street, then it -- that it was so. However, the maps that were shown to me, as well as this list, is something that I don't know whether it tallies with the facts, but I'm certain that I was in that part of the neighbourhood and that I carried out that on-site investigation. What the name of the street was, Nehru's or Hamdije Kapidzica, that I don't know any longer. The name must have been on the signs there, but we would not have written down "Nehru's Street" if it weren't so. I am not privy to any street names changes, and I don't know what the date of the map is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, this is an official web site of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is an official document of the state, in which they publish street names changes; in particular, in the case of the municipality of Novi Grad in Sarajevo. This Defence is 100 certain [as interpreted] that it is what it purports to be. We are simply looking for a way to produce it in the courtroom. It was confirmed that the old name was Nehru's Street and the new is Hamdije Kapidzica Street, and another witness marked a completely different building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is an older map and that perhaps it is Hamdije Kapidzica Street. There are far more precise maps, which is also something I use in my work. They are far better, compared to this one, and there is no problem in producing those. You can even use the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is taken off the internet, from a web site of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Hamdije Kapidzica Street used to be called Nehru's Street. You agree, therefore, that on the report, it says "Nehru's Street 10"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If that's what the report says, and I believe I saw a moment ago that it is Nehru's Street 10, although I wasn't shown the report itself - perhaps you could - if it says it is Nehru's Street 10, that is where the on-site investigation was performed. It was at the location I marked previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, having seen the map, you are confident as to the location of the incident that took place, whatever the name of the street was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not exclude the possibility that you were mistaken -- might have been mistaken with the street name at the time when producing the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why I said that I would like to read this. I think that the very same address is on all reports. I think that -- this incident took place 15 or 16 years ago, but I think I do remember that I went to the scene with some trepidation, so I think it is where I marked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we up-load Exhibit D893.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So my question for you, Mr. Karadzic, that I posed earlier on. So my question was how the Hamdije Kapidzica Street could be parallel to Miroslava Krleze Street, which is 293 on this map. And you see Hamdije Kapidzica is perpendicular to that street to the north. So I didn't understand your question, that Hamdije Kapidzica Street is the third street parallel to this one. What did you mean at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, not Miroslava Krleze, but Mimar Sinana and Kurta Sorta. It is parallel to Kurta Sorta, as marked by this witness. However, we have Mr. Sabljica's testimony on the map, on an exhibit that was admitted, he marked with precision this building in Hamdije Kapidzica Street. If you remember, we established that it is not from the south to the east, but from the south to the west. And the report says that the apartment was oriented north-east, but it was established here, beyond any doubt, that the building, as a whole, was oriented towards the south-west and the north-east; the other side, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On transcript page 63, line 24 onward, you said: "Miroslava Krleze is the one you marked, and Hamdije Kapidzica is the third street parallel to it, it is longitudinal to the first street." Probably there may have been a mistake in the translation, but let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I thought that "longitudinal" is sufficient, but transversal is perpendicular, so the third longitudinal is parallel. Oh, I see. This was confirmed by one of the witnesses from this list. Can we have the report once again, because the witness asked for it. Can we cast a glance again at 65 ter 09766. We don't want to have it broadcast, because we'll be referring to names. Please focus on number 2. Number 2 testified as a protected witness, and he marked, with precision, the location of the building, and he established that the report misstates that it is oriented towards the south-west, rather than the south-east, as the report says. Let me just remind you, Excellencies, that playing with cardinal points is the main element of wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) A few moments ago, you mentioned the ballistics expert, Mirza Sabljica. I don't see him here. And it says in the report, itself, "Nehruova number 10," that this is an official report that was compiled by the inspector whose name is listed under number 2. However, my report is not there. There should be the proper photo file of this same investigation that would explain certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: All of that had been sent. It should be before this Court. I do not see my own report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we go back to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have five minutes for today, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your official note, Witness, it says that everything is as stated in the official report, and this is the only official report from this incident; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: This is the official report that was compiled by the witness who had already appeared here. But my report should be there as well, the report of the crime technician, and together with this, it would constitute a single file. But I don't see my own report at all. I keep looking at the official report that was compiled by the member of the team who was together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't quite understand what you are saying. Are you making a parallel report or an official note that is incorporated into this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I work on a parallel report, on a crime technician's report, and I work on the photo file. And perhaps I even draw the actual scene if the judge asks me to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since a general was found guilty of this incident, although it was not included in the indictment, could we please have everything we need by tomorrow; the report of this witness, the photographs, so that we fully elucidate the matter. We're going to find the exhibit as well, I mean, the testimony of number 2 and the map that he marked. Please, Excellencies, could you support this? Can we have all of this by tomorrow, everything that is relevant in terms of ruling on this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you changed something here in these statements, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Subsequently, you said that you remembered that you used a string to establish the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: If I said so, that should be recorded in my report. As far as I can remember, and this is even in my diary, which is accessible, it says exactly what I did. I even mentioned the height, and also I said that all the measurements were done at the scene, itself. As far as I can see in the report that is before me, these measurements are there. So I did the measuring in the presence of the entire team that was there with me on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your amalgamated statement, paragraph 81, you say that on the 15th of May, you carried out an investigation of the incident that happened on the 14th of May, 15 minutes before midnight, and you say that the on-site investigation was supposed to be a typical one. On the following day -- et cetera. The bullet arrived -- came through a window, and then you say how the victim's body was hit - if you have the report, please look at it - and: [In English] "We took a piece of string and connected these two points, and we were able to establish the exact trajectory of the bullet. The bullet came from Dobrinja 1. That means from apartment buildings in Dobrinja 1 neighbourhood. That was -- that area was under the Army of Republika Srpska." [Interpretation] In the previous statements, you did not mention this, also not in the reports, you did not say that you used a string. But you did say that your diary actually reminded you of what had happened; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I cannot remember what it was that jogged my memory. Everything is contained in my report. This is one of the cases where this string is produced, where we have several points involved in the damage caused by the bullet. I remember another case that I worked on. And on the basis of these points, I could establish where the bullet had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How can we see part of your statement -- or, rather, your report, the page that refers to that? Can we place it on the ELMO? Can we put it on the ELMO, that page from your diary? Can we see what it says there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: You mean the photocopy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Well, go ahead. I would like to ask whether something could be done. Could I have a look at something? In my diary, in addition to this, there are some other things that are not relevant to this trial. Can we just show the part that is relevant to this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't have to be broadcast. We can cover it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not broadcast. Yes, Mr. Gaynor. If the witness is -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I have the original of the witness's diary. Perhaps I could return it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that would be more convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in closed session, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we are in public session. But if necessary -- we do not broadcast the content of that diary, so nothing is broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I see the photocopy of part of my diary here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what is your question, Mr. Karadzic? That will be your last one for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is written here? Does it say that you used a string to measure this? You can read all of it to the Trial Chamber, if you wish, or you can indicate what it was that jogged your memory to the effect that you forgot to write this in your first report.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: First I'm going to clarify what this diary is. It contains all my on-site investigations from November 1993, I think, until 1996, I think. Inter alia, there is this particular case as well. My diary was used for note-taking, to remind me how I'm going to type up the report ultimately. It does not reflect everything I did at the scene, itself. These were specific notes that I used to type up the official report. Actually, I can read this to you: "The 15th of May, 1995 ..." "Murder, Nehruova 10/4." And then it says "Tabakovic, Jasmina," so it has to do with that young girl. And then it says: "On the 24th of May, 1995, at 2345 hours, from the direction of Dobrinja 1, a gunshot that came from a rifle killed Jasmina Tabakovic in an apartment on Jawaharlal Nehru 10/4 (1969)," which is the year of her birth: "The bullet passed through the window at a height of 116 centimetres. Then the curtain was at 116.5 centimetres and hit Jasmina in the area of the left breast. The bullet went out through the -- exited through the area of the right shoulder blade and went through the wardrobe and -- at a height of 124 centimetres, and exited from it at a height of 131 centimetres, and stopped at the level of 132 centimetres. The body was transferred to the morgue." And then the names are registered there, the members of the team. I don't know whether I was working at Novi Grad Station at the time or whether I was at the other Security Services Centre. On the basis of this reminder, I wrote up the crime technician's report that I don't have on the screen here, and all of this should be in it. When I was saying that I was measuring the height on the sheet, on the window, and everywhere else, in such a situation you always use a string in order to carry out that measurement. However, I didn't have to write that in my diary, that a string was used for it. It simply had to be done in order to establish where the bullet had come from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So let us try to finish this. Excellencies, let us try to finish this so we don't wait until tomorrow. I just have two extra questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of what you wrote here, does it seem obvious that the bullet is ascending? It entering at 116 centimetres, and then goes to 116.5 centimetres, and then goes to 124, and then 131, and then 132. Is the bullet going up?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: Logically, it would seem so. From 116 to 132 on the wall, it means an ascending trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish the angle at which the bullet arrived?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3044.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we do that tomorrow, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Okay, okay. [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll be resuming tomorrow morning at 9.00.
